entries.title: US insurance giant Allstate has been suffering an outage since November 23, affecting its website and app; the company hasn't said what is causing the outage (Jean Eaglesham/Wall Street Journal)
Some users claim Claude is silently sabotaging projects, but the behavior may stem from a clash between its proactive nature and strict instruction following (Drew Breunig)
Q&A with AI researchers Ege Erdil and Daniel Kokotajlo on the odds of an intelligence explosion before 2029, pausing AI, the US antagonizing China, and more (Dwarkesh Patel/Dwarkesh Podcast)
OpenAI countersues Apple for allegedly stealing trade secrets via a staffer who returned to Apple and "coercing and threatening" suppliers that work with both (Financial Times)
Sources: Verizon is in talks to buy fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for ~$6B, as part of its goal to expand its network to 50M US homes and businesses (Financial Times)
European Central Bank survey: 44% of employed EU consumers reported using AI weekly at work in August, on par with US peers; 18% used it daily, above US levels (Alexander Weber/Bloomberg)
SAP confirms a cybersecurity incident; report: hackers obtained its staffers' authentication tokens, letting them copy and alter source code stored on GitHub (Eduard Kovacs/SecurityWeek)
The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)
Interviews with Huawei CEO Ren Zhengfei and others on how Trump's restrictions pushed Huawei toward self-reliance, making it central to China's AI ambitions (New York Times)
Serial numbers in Chinese filings reveal that Nvidia's restricted Blackwell chips were installed at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang and Megaspeed (Bloomberg)
Meituan reports Q3 revenue up 21.6% YoY to ~$17.3B, above est., and an adjusted net profit of ~$285.1M, up from a ~$2.4B adjusted net loss (Ben Jiang/South China Morning Post)
Sources: the US Air Force recently discovered a breach of Cloud One, which combines Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Google clouds to power Air Force applications (Reuters)
A look at proposals for vertical data centers, often the only option where land is limited in places like Taiwan; Kansas City recently rejected a 20-story tower (Tiffany Hsu/New York Times)
Foreign investors sold a record net $33.1B of Taiwanese stocks in November, topping October's record outflow amid AI valuation fears and a broader tech sell-off (Eunice Xu/Bloomberg)
US smartphone shipments fell 9% YoY in Q3 as memory costs hit Android OEMs, especially at the low end; Apple's share rose from 50% to 57%, Samsung held at 25% (Maurice Klaehne/Counterpoint Research)
